Ripple Continues Massive RLUSD Minting Spree on XRPL
Luke Dashjr exits mining pool Ocean after split over Bitcoin mining’s future
Cronos halts blockchain after $75 million lending exploit hits lending app Tectonic
September Fed rate hike fears look overblown as the probability stands at just 58%, not 90%

en.title: Cronos Halted, XRP Shorts Pile Up, Fed Hike Odds Cut: A Pivotal Crypto Morning
en.body:
Crypto markets woke up to a turbulent mix of security incidents, derivatives positioning and shifting macro signals. The largest shock came from Cronos, where validators paused the blockchain after a roughly $75 million lending exploit struck decentralized lending app Tectonic. According to CoinDesk, an attacker allegedly inflated the thinly traded TONIC token by 100-fold, used it as inflated collateral to borrow real assets, and left most funds stranded once the network froze. The incident highlights how low-liquidity collateral markets remain a structural weak point across DeFi protocols, and traders are watching for an official post-mortem from Cronos and Tectonic teams in the coming days.

On a brighter note, Ripple continues aggressive stablecoin expansion. U.Today reports that Ripple has minted millions of additional RLUSD tokens across the XRP Ledger and Ethereum over the past several days, pushing the dollar-pegged asset's total supply above $2 billion. The minting spree signals sustained institutional demand for a regulated, on-chain dollar and reinforces the broader push by payment-focused networks to capture stablecoin market share.

Meanwhile, XRP derivatives positioning is drawing fresh attention. CryptoSlate points to a CFTC snapshot from August 25 showing approximately 115.7 million XRP-equivalent net short positions sitting against rising dealer and asset-manager net longs. Such a lopsided setup means a sharp upward move could force short liquidations, amplifying any breakout. On-chain volume on XRP pairs has ticked higher this week, and traders are monitoring the $0.65 resistance zone as a potential trigger.

In the Bitcoin ecosystem, CoinDesk reports that developer Luke Dashjr has departed mining pool Ocean following a mutual split over the future direction of Bitcoin mining and protocol development. The departure, while philosophical rather than technical, removes one of the more vocal contributors from a pool that has positioned itself around filterable block templates and ordinals-friendly policies.

Finally, macro sentiment got a softer read. CoinDesk notes that the implied probability of a September Fed rate hike now sits around 58 percent, well below the 90 percent figure circulating earlier in the week after Kevin Warsh's hawkish remarks. $ETH futures open interest rose modestly as traders pared back tightening bets, while $BTC continues to consolidate near recent highs with the 200-day moving average acting as support.
